declarations.description:
The usual question when something has to be decided about several things («overwrite this file?»): it asks about each one in a dialog, with the progress («2 of 5»), and the answer can be
«yes to all» (or «no to all») for the rest, or cancelling, so that nothing happens. It knows nothing of what it asks: whoever uses it gives the verbs (`labels`) and how each thing is named
(`describe`). It is a `wa-dialog` inside, so it opens and closes like one: the `open` property, `show()` and `hide()`, `light-dismiss`, Escape, and the events of Web Awesome that
its dialog fires, which come out of this element as they are (`wa-show`, `wa-after-show`, `wa-hide` and `wa-after-hide`, the first and the third cancellable). Enter is the first button (the positive verb). It knows nothing of the Back button: whoever wants Back to
cancel it listens to those events (`BackClose.bind` in webutils).

```html
<wax-ask-each label="Overwrite?" question="Overwrite"></wax-ask-each>
```
```js
askEach.describe = file => `«${file.name}»`;
askEach.labels = { yes: 'Overwrite', no: 'Skip', yesAll: 'Overwrite all', noAll: 'Skip all' };
const answers = await askEach.ask(files);   // an array of booleans in the order of the files (true is the positive verb), or null if it was cancelled
```

declarations.description:
A box to choose from a list with a search box to filter it by typing: what a `<select>` with many options should be. It is a Web Awesome `wa-select` whose first child is a
search box (a `wa-input`): when it opens the focus goes to the box, typing hides the options that do not match, and the arrows pass from the box to the options that are seen. It is
used where a `<select>` would go: it has `value`, `disabled`, `name` and `required`, takes part in a form, and fires `change` when something is chosen. It chooses only among what it
has: what is typed is for searching, it is not kept. It knows nothing of what the choices are or of any language: everything comes by property. It imports the Web Awesome components it uses (`wa-select`, `wa-option`, `wa-input`).

```html
<wax-combobox placeholder="Pick one..." empty-text="Nothing matches"></wax-combobox>
```
```js
combo.choices = [{ value: 'es', label: 'España' }, { value: 'fr', label: 'Francia' }];   // before the value: a value that is not among the choices is dropped
combo.value = 'es';
combo.addEventListener('change', () => use(combo.value));
```

If the choices are not all there and have to be fetched as the user types, listen to `wax-query` and give the new `choices`.

declarations.description:
A card that floats next to what was clicked: in a long list the thing it talks about may be far away, out of sight. With a mouse it can also peek: it shows a moment after the pointer
arrives (`peek`), goes when it leaves (`leave`), and stays once clicked (`show`); clicking the same thing again closes it (`toggle`). Without a mouse there is no "next to": it goes in the
middle with the rest dimmed. Escape, a click outside and its × close it too.

It opens and closes like a `wa-dialog`: the `open` property, `show()` and `hide()`, and the four events of Web Awesome (`wa-show`, `wa-after-show`, `wa-hide` and `wa-after-hide`, its own
classes). `wa-show` and `wa-hide` can be cancelled (`preventDefault()` keeps it as it was); at `wa-show` the element already has its `anchor` and its `centered`. It knows nothing of what it shows: the content is its children, which whoever opens it fills in the listener of
`wa-show` (and cancels it if there is nothing to say). It knows nothing of the Back button either: whoever wants Back to close it listens to its events.

```html
<wax-floating-card close-label="Cerrar"></wax-floating-card>   <!-- a child of the body -->
```
```js
card.addEventListener('wa-show', event => {                       // the content, when it is going to show (the events of what is inside come up here too: look at event.target)
  if (event.target === card) card.replaceChildren(dayView(card.anchor.dataset.day));
});
day.addEventListener('click', () => card.toggle(day));            // pinned, next to the day; the same day again closes it
day.addEventListener('mouseenter', () => card.peek(day));         // with a mouse, after a moment
day.addEventListener('mouseleave', () => card.leave());
```

It is placed with the coordinates of the page, so it has to be a child of the `body` (or of an element that is not positioned).

declarations.description:
The usual list to choose from: icon, name and a note per line. One line is selected at a time (click it again to clear), and with Ctrl, Cmd or Shift + click
lines are marked, any number, for the application to do something with them (join them). It knows nothing about what the items are.

```html
<wax-item-list empty="Nothing here"></wax-item-list>
```
```js
list.items = sites.map(s => ({ key: s.id, icon: '🍺', name: s.name, note: `${s.meters} m`, faded: s.hidden }));
list.addEventListener('wax-select', event => open(event.detail.key));   // key is null when the selection is cleared
list.addEventListener('wax-mark', event => join(event.detail.keys));
```

Two things a list can also do, if asked:
- **Move** (`movable`): each line has a handle, dragged with mouse or finger, or moved with the arrow keys when it has the focus; the list gives back the keys in their
  new order (`wax-move`).
- **Swipe** (`swipe-label`): sliding a line sideways with the finger uncovers one action (Remove, Seen) instead of doing it straight away (`wax-swipe`).

declarations.description:
The block that repeats in the screens that edit things: the filters (if any), the search box, the «New» button and, below, the list of what there is, where one entry is chosen (clicking the chosen one again does not clear it). The button is always above the list, in case it is long. It knows nothing of what the entries are or how they are filtered: whoever uses it gives what is to be shown (`items`) when what is typed changes (`wax-query`). The list is a ``, whose parts are exported. ```html
...
 ``` ```js manager.items = [{ key: 'a', name: 'One', icon: '🏆', note: 'a note' }]; manager.addEventListener('wax-select', event => open(event.detail.key)); manager.addEventListener('wax-new', () => openNew()); manager.addEventListener('wax-query', () => manager.items = filter(manager.query)); ```
